metadata.name: Pneumonia (community-acquired)
metadata.emergency_level: Can be an emergency - severity-assessed (CRB-65/CURB-65); sepsis is life-threatening
metadata.severity: Ranges from mild (home) to severe (ICU); a leading infectious cause of death

overview.short_description: Acute infection of the lung parenchyma causing cough, fever, breathlessness and pleuritic pain, with focal chest signs and (where imaged) consolidation, requiring severity assessment to guide treatment setting.
overview.detailed_description: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is common and potentially life-threatening. Diagnosis is clinical (symptoms + focal chest signs), supported by chest X-ray where available. The central task is severity assessment (CRB-65 in the community, CURB-65 in hospital) to decide home vs hospital care, prompt antibiotics, and recognition of sepsis. Streptococcus pneumoniae is the commonest cause.
overview.pathophysiology: Pathogens reach distal airways/alveoli, provoking an inflammatory exudate that fills alveoli (consolidation), impairing gas exchange and causing hypoxia, systemic inflammatory response and sometimes sepsis.
overview.etiology: Bacterial (Streptococcus pneumoniae most common; also Haemophilus influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydophila, Legionella, Staphylococcus aureus) and viral (influenza, SARS-CoV-2, RSV). Aspiration in those with swallowing impairment.
overview.natural_history: Fever/symptoms improve over days with effective treatment; radiographic changes lag and can persist weeks. Complications include effusion/empyema, sepsis and respiratory failure.
overview.prognosis: Good in low-severity CAP treated promptly; mortality rises with age, comorbidity and severity (CURB-65).

prevalence.value: A common cause of primary-care and hospital presentations; incidence rises with age.

incidence.value: Higher in winter and in the very young and elderly.

mortality.value: A leading infectious cause of death worldwide; low in mild CAP, high in severe/elderly (WHO).

epidemiology.age_groups: Extremes of age at highest risk.

risk_factors.smoking: Major risk factor; impairs mucociliary defence.
risk_factors.hypertension: Not a direct risk factor; cardiovascular comorbidity worsens outcomes.
risk_factors.occupation: Certain exposures (e.g., Legionella from water systems).
risk_factors.medications: Immunosuppressants, inhaled/oral steroids, acid suppression (aspiration), sedatives (aspiration).
risk_factors.previous_diseases: COPD/asthma, heart failure, chronic kidney/liver disease, neurological disease with swallowing impairment, immunosuppression, recent influenza.

chief_complaints.importance: May be the main sign in the elderly

symptoms.importance: Systemic infection; may be absent in the elderly

symptoms.symptom: Focal chest signs (crackles, bronchial breathing, dullness)
symptoms.importance: Focal signs strongly support pneumonia over bronchitis
Severity marker (CRB-65) and may be presenting sign in elderly

symptoms.symptom: Hypotension, marked hypoxia, cyanosis, severe tachypnoea (severe/sepsis)

negative_findings.finding: No focal chest signs, normal saturations, not tachypnoeic, systemically well
negative_findings.why_important: Makes pneumonia much less likely and supports acute bronchitis (usually no antibiotics)
Argues strongly against pneumonia (though early X-rays can lag)

history_questions.question: Do you have cough with fever, breathlessness, and chest pain, and how quickly did it start?
How breathless are you, and can you manage at home (oral intake, support)?
Any comorbidity (COPD, heart failure, diabetes, immunosuppression) or recent travel/influenza?
history_questions.why_ask: Risk stratification and atypical pathogen clues

history_questions.question: Any features of sepsis (very unwell, confusion, low output, cold/clammy)?

physical_examination.expected_finding: Focal crackles, bronchial breathing, dullness to percussion

physical_examination.examination: Blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, mental state (CRB-65 components)

physical_examination.expected_finding: Assess ability to manage at home

vital_signs.temperature: Often raised (may be normal/low in elderly or severe sepsis)
vital_signs.blood_pressure: Low BP (e.g., diastolic <=60) is a severity/sepsis marker
vital_signs.respiratory_rate: Raised RR (>=30) is a severity marker
vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: May be reduced; hypoxia indicates severity

laboratory_tests.indication: To confirm pneumonia where diagnosis uncertain or in hospital

laboratory_tests.test_name: CRP / FBC / U&E (CURB-65 uses urea) / blood cultures
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Raised inflammatory markers; urea for CURB-65

laboratory_tests.test_name: Pulse oximetry / blood gas; sputum, urinary antigens (pneumococcal/Legionella), viral PCR
laboratory_tests.indication: Severity and microbiology in moderate-severe CAP

imaging.when_needed: Confirm diagnosis/complications (standard in hospital; selectively in community)
imaging.expected_findings: Lobar or patchy consolidation; parapneumonic effusion

ecg.when_needed: If cardiac comorbidity/complication or severe illness
ecg.findings: Sinus tachycardia; assess arrhythmia/ischaemia in comorbidity.

other_diagnostic_tests.culture: Sputum and blood cultures in moderate-severe CAP; pleural fluid if effusion
other_diagnostic_tests.pcr: Respiratory viral PCR (influenza, SARS-CoV-2) where relevant

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Clinical CAP: symptoms of an acute lower respiratory tract infection (cough plus at least one of fever, breathlessness, pleuritic pain, focal chest signs) with NEW focal chest signs and/or radiographic consolidation, in a patient not hospitalised. Assess severity with CRB-65 (community) or CURB-65 (hospital).

diagnostic_scores.value: CRB-65 (1 point each): Confusion; Respiratory rate >=30; Blood pressure (systolic <90 or diastolic <=60); age >=65. CURB-65 adds Urea >7 mmol/L.

cutoff_values.value: CRB-65: 0 low risk (consider home), 1-2 intermediate, 3-4 high risk (urgent hospital assessment). CURB-65: 0-1 low, 2 moderate, 3-5 high severity.

differential_diagnosis.differences: No focal chest signs/consolidation, systemically well
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Are there focal chest signs or breathlessness/high fever?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Known airway disease, wheeze-predominant, no consolidation
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Do you have known COPD/asthma and is it wheeze-predominant?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Often less fever/sputum, risk factors (immobility, surgery, malignancy), sudden onset
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Sudden dyspnoea, pleuritic pain, leg swelling
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Sudden breathlessness with risk factors and little sputum?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Orthopnoea, oedema, cardiac history, bilateral basal crackles
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Breathless lying flat with ankle swelling?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Non-resolving on repeat imaging, weight loss, haemoptysis, smoker
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any weight loss or coughing blood, and does it resolve?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are there focal chest signs, high fever, breathlessness, or hypoxia (rather than a well patient with just a cough)?
Do you have confusion, a fast breathing rate, low blood pressure, or are you 65+?

next_best_question.question: What is your CRB-65 (confusion, RR>=30, low BP, age>=65), oxygen level, and can you cope at home?
next_best_question.branching_logic: CRB-65 0 and well/normal SpO2 -> home antibiotics + safety-net; CRB-65 1-2 or hypoxia/comorbidity -> consider hospital; CRB-65 3-4 or sepsis -> urgent hospital admission

red_flags.finding: Signs of sepsis: confusion, RR >=30, SpO2 <92%, systolic BP <90, mottled/cold, reduced urine output
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - sepsis pathway: oxygen, fluids, urgent antibiotics, hospital admission

red_flags.finding: Haemoptysis, weight loss, or non-resolving consolidation
red_flags.immediate_action: Investigate for malignancy/other pathology (repeat imaging, refer)

red_flags.finding: Large pleural effusion / suspected empyema (persistent fever, sepsis)

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Moderate-high severity CAP (CRB-65/CURB-65), hypoxia, sepsis, inability to cope at home, or significant comorbidity - hospital assessment.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Non-resolving pneumonia for further investigation (exclude malignancy); recurrent pneumonia in the same area.

initial_management.supportive_care: Severity assessment (CRB-65/CURB-65), oxygen to target saturations, fluids/antipyretics, and choosing the correct treatment setting.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Severity- and setting-directed antibiotic; Paracetamol; Antiviral. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG250.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Rest, fluids, smoking cessation; safety-net advice on deterioration; ensure follow-up.
initial_management.follow_up: Review response at ~48-72 hours; arrange follow-up chest X-ray at ~6 weeks for those at higher risk of malignancy (e.g., smokers, >50) to confirm resolution.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Prompt antibiotics guided by severity and local guidance: low-severity CAP usually amoxicillin (or a macrolide/doxycycline if penicillin-allergic); moderate-high severity uses broader/combination regimens per local policy. Start within recommended timeframes, especially in severe disease/sepsis. Add antiviral/other cover where indicated (e.g., influenza).

patient_education.home_advice: Pneumonia is a lung infection that usually needs antibiotics. If you are being treated at home, take the full course, rest, drink fluids, and use paracetamol for fever. It is important to know the danger signs. Get emergency help if you become confused, very breathless, your lips turn blue, you can't keep fluids down, or you feel you are getting worse.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: الالتهاب الرئوي عدوى في الرئة تحتاج عادةً إلى مضادات حيوية. إن كنت تُعالَج في المنزل، أكمل الجرعة كاملة وارتَح واشرب السوائل واستخدم الباراسيتامول للحرارة. من المهم معرفة علامات الخطر. اطلب المساعدة الطارئة إذا حدث تشوّش، أو ضيق نفس شديد، أو ازرقّت الشفتان، أو لم تستطع الاحتفاظ بالسوائل، أو شعرت أنك تزداد سوءاً.
patient_education.prevention: Smoking cessation; influenza and pneumococcal vaccination for at-risk groups.
patient_education.warning_signs: Confusion, severe breathlessness, blue lips, high or persistent fever, inability to keep fluids down, or feeling markedly worse - seek emergency care.

prevention.vaccination: Pneumococcal and influenza (and COVID-19) vaccination for at-risk groups reduces incidence/severity.
prevention.lifestyle: Smoking cessation; good nutrition; manage comorbidity.

evidence.evidence_level: High for severity-guided management and prompt antibiotics; high for vaccination in prevention.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG250; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE NG250, BTS CAP guideline, IDSA/ATS.

limitations: Guidelines require individual clinical judgement and may differ by country, formulary and antimicrobial resistance.
The evidence audit verifies traceability and major safety structure; it does not certify every narrative sentence.
No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Assess severity promptly, start appropriate antimicrobials and detect respiratory failure/sepsis.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Severity- and setting-directed antibiotic; Paracetamol; Antiviral. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG250.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Hydration, smoking cessation and safety-netting; oxygen/fluids are prescribed to physiological targets in monitored care.

medication_options.when_to_consider: After clinical diagnosis and severity assessment
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: documented immediate or severe delayed penicillin allergy
use_caution_if: renal impairment, prior C. difficile, or recent antibiotic exposure
monitoring: clinical response, allergy and antibiotic-associated diarrhoea

avoid_if: prior serious macrolide allergy or clinically important QT prolongation with interacting drugs
use_caution_if: liver disease, bradycardia, hypokalaemia, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy, or QT-prolonging medicines
monitoring: clinical response; ECG/electrolytes when risk is material

avoid_if: pregnancy, breastfeeding where unsuitable, or tetracycline allergy
use_caution_if: oesophageal disease, liver disease, photosensitivity, or interacting iron/calcium/antacid products
monitoring: clinical response and gastrointestinal/photosensitivity adverse effects

medication_options.clinical_note: Use current local formulary, resistance data, allergy history and renal/hepatic dosing; do not hard-code one regimen for all patients.

medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: severe active liver disease or prior serious reaction
use_caution_if: heavy alcohol use, malnutrition, low body weight, or concomitant paracetamol-containing products
monitoring: total daily exposure and clinical response

medication_options.when_to_consider: Influenza or other treatable virus when indicated
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: renal impairment, severe vomiting, or neuropsychiatric history
monitoring: dose adjustment by renal function, clinical response, nausea/vomiting

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Urgent hospital care for high severity, hypoxia, sepsis, confusion, hypotension, inability to take oral treatment or rapid deterioration.
